responsibilities.name: Weekly Cost Anomaly Check
responsibilities.instruction: Check GCP billing data for cost anomalies and spikes. Compare this week's costs against the previous 4-week average. Flag any service or project with a significant cost increase. Produce a cost anomaly report.

context.purpose: Detect unexpected cost spikes before they accumulate into large overruns. GCP costs can spike from misconfigured services, runaway queries, or forgotten resources. Weekly monitoring catches these within 7 days.
process: STEP 1 — Read MEMORY.md to get the billing export table location, project list, and any known cost baselines.
STEP 2 — Query the billing export for the current week's costs by service and project.
STEP 3 — Query the billing export for the previous 4-week rolling average by service and project.
STEP 4 — Calculate the variance: (current_week - 4wk_avg) / 4wk_avg * 100 for each line item.
STEP 5 — Apply variance thresholds: >15% = WARNING, >30% = HIGH, >50% = CRITICAL.
STEP 6 — For any HIGH or CRITICAL items, drill into the top SKUs to identify the root cause.
STEP 7 — Produce the anomaly report: service, project, current cost, baseline cost, variance %, severity, likely cause.
STEP 8 — If CRITICAL anomalies found, escalate immediately. Otherwise log findings to MEMORY.md.
context.success_criteria: All GCP costs are within expected ranges, or anomalies are identified with root cause attribution, severity classification, and recommended next steps.
context.prior_learnings: Billing export data lags 24-48 hours — run this on Monday to capture the full prior week. First-of-month invoices can cause false positives due to CUD or SUD true-ups. Committed use discount charges appear as lump sums — exclude them from anomaly detection or handle separately.

responsibilities.name: Monthly Cost Close & Variance Report
responsibilities.instruction: Produce the monthly cost summary and variance report. Summarize total GCP spend by service and project for the previous month. Compare against budget and the prior month. Generate a variance analysis with root cause attribution for significant changes.

context.purpose: Provide a structured monthly financial close for GCP costs. This report is the primary financial artifact for stakeholder review, budget tracking, and forecasting. Consistent monthly cadence enables trend analysis.
process: STEP 1 — Read MEMORY.md to get the billing export table, budget targets, and prior month's summary for comparison.
STEP 2 — Query the billing export for the previous calendar month's total costs, grouped by service and project.
STEP 3 — Query for credits (CUDs, SUDs, promotional) separately and net them against gross costs.
STEP 4 — Compare actuals to budget: calculate absolute ($) and relative (%) variance per line item.
STEP 5 — Compare actuals to prior month: calculate month-over-month change per line item.
STEP 6 — For any variance >5% or >$100, apply the variance analysis framework: identify, quantify, attribute, classify, recommend.
STEP 7 — Produce the monthly close report with sections: Executive Summary, Cost by Service, Cost by Project, Budget vs Actual, Month-over-Month, Top Variances, Recommendations.
STEP 8 — Update MEMORY.md with the new month's totals as the baseline for next month's comparison.
STEP 9 — If total spend exceeded budget by >10%, escalate to user with the report and recommendations.
context.success_criteria: A complete monthly cost report with: total spend, service breakdown, project breakdown, budget variance, MoM variance, attribution for top variances, and actionable recommendations. All numbers traceable to billing export queries.
context.prior_learnings: Run on the 1st but billing data for the last 1-2 days of the prior month may not be finalized — note the data freshness caveat in the report. CUD charges can distort single-month views — present both gross and net-of-CUD views. Some projects may be new and lack a prior month baseline — handle these as 'New' rather than infinite variance.
